question: The Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) has been a key financial instrument for investment in ports in the TEN-T network, improving competitiveness and energy efficiency and cutting emissions.

The TEN-T network, however, is mainly based on civilian transport corridors and, as things stand, it does not take sufficient account of the role of ports in terms of security of supply, the logistics of critical raw materials or military mobility.

This is particularly the case in Finland, where, owing to low levels of traffic, not all ports of national importance are included in the TEN-T network, even though they are of strategic importance. The TEN-T Regulation, which entered into force in summer 2024, allows for a reassessment of parts of the network, but the Commission has not yet taken any action in this direction. 1.

Does the Commission intend to reassess the list of ports included in the TEN-T network before the start of the next multiannual financial framework, so that the geostrategic importance, security of supply and military mobility needs of the ports concerned are better recognised?

How will the Commission ensure that ports that are essential for military mobility are eligible for CEF funding even when they are not currently part of the TEN-T core network or the comprehensive network?
Does the Commission intend to ensure that more consideration is given to security of supply in EU transport policy, alongside military mobility?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.3.2026) The list of ports included in the trans-European transport network (TEN-T) was revised recently as part of the broader review of the TEN-T framework, reflected in Regulation (EU) 2024/16791. The entry criteria for ports and other nodes go beyond pure traffic-volume considerations.

They are detailed in Article 25(4) of the regulation and the TEN-T planning methodology2. Article 58 of the regulation allows amendments to the network by means of delegated acts. However, considering the recent revision and the absence of requests for additions from Member States, the Commission currently has no plans for such amendments but is continuously monitoring the situation.

The eligibility of ports for funding under the Connecting Europe Facility military mobility envelope relies – inter alia – on their location within the TEN-T and military mobility network. Therefore, for eligibility, non TEN-T ports would need to be included through the means of Article 58, as outlined above.

The TEN-T policy promotes a sustainable, safe, efficient and resilient network by – inter alia – improving connectivity, upgrading rail links, reducing dwelling times, and strengthening intermodal capacity. This supports more reliable logistics and supply chains. Almost 75% of goods entering or leaving Europe go through EU ports, making them critical for European supply chains.
This is set to be addressed further by the European Ports Strategy and EU Industrial Maritime Strategy.
